name: A time-parameterised LR schedule with a fixed rate overshoots when throughput rises
statement: Under a wall-clock budget the LR schedule is a function of elapsed time, so its shape is invariant to throughput. The number of updates taken along that shape is not: a faster host completes more steps, and total parameter movement scales as N * mean_lr. With no term adapting the rate to N -- the AdamW groups are rescaled by model width, the Muon matrix LR by nothing -- extra throughput becomes extra movement, and past a threshold the run overshoots and val_bpb rises even though more tokens were seen.

nodes.label: host throughput, or any change that buys steps
optimizer steps N completed in the 300s budget

assumptions.statement: The threshold is a property of the LR magnitude and N, not of the quiet host that produced the high-step runs. Step count and contention were perfectly confounded in the n=2 evidence, and this is the weakest link.

alternatives: A quiet host changes something else -- clocks, cache residency, neighbour interference -- and step count is a bystander.
The degradation is a data-order effect at 0.82 epochs rather than an optimization effect.
Muon specifically mis-behaves at higher update counts, independent of the LR magnitude.
predictions: Damping the LR by 1/sqrt(N) removes the penalty at >750 steps and leaves <750 steps unchanged.
Throttling a quiet host to ~650 steps WITHOUT the damping should also remove the penalty, which separates steps from contention.
Any candidate that buys steps -- attention span, window pattern, kernel work -- inherits this penalty and will read worse than it is.
falsifiers: Damping does not recover the penalty at >750 steps.
A throttled quiet host still shows the penalty at ~650 steps, indicting contention rather than steps.
Damping changes val_bpb below 750 steps, where the clamp makes it a no-op.
